extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when multiple claimed inventions in a single US patent application are distinct/independent, when an examiner may require restriction/election, and the procedures for withdrawing restriction, rejoinder, and applicant rebuttal under MPEP and 35 U.S.C. 121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration on Allowance of Elected Combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determining that all claims directed to an elected combination invention are allowable, the examiner must reconsider the propriety of the restriction requirement and, where the combination is allowable in view of the patentability of at least one subcombination, withdraw the restriction requirement between the elected combination and patentable subcombination(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawn, any subcombinations that were searched and determined to be allowable must be rejoined. If a subcombination is elected and determined allowable, nonelected claims requiring all the limitations of the allowable claim will be rejoined in accordance with MPEP § 821.04. Use form paragraph 8.21 (and form paragraph 8.21.04 where applicable) to conclude restriction requirements and to notify applicant about potential rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness of Subcombinations Usable Together
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcombinations disclosed as usable together in a single combination are distinct if they do not overlap in scope, are not obvious variants, and at least one subcombination is separately usable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must show, by way of example, that one of the subcombinations has utility other than in the disclosed combination. Use form paragraph 8.16 to make restriction requirements between subcombinations and conclude with form paragraph 8.21. Applicant is advised that claims in continuations/divisionals anticipated by or including all limitations of an allowable claim may be subject to double patenting rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and Apparatus Distinctness Test
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed process and an apparatus for its practice are distinct if either (A) the process as claimed can be practiced by another materially different apparatus or by hand, or (B) the apparatus as claimed can be used to practice another materially different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.17 may be used for restriction between process and apparatus. Examiner should provide reasonable examples that recite material differences (example need not be documented). If applicant proves or convincingly argues there is no material difference or that the process cannot be performed by hand, the burden shifts to the examiner to document another materially different process or apparatus or withdraw the requirement. Conclude with form paragraph 8.21; follow with form paragraph 8.21.04 when applicable to notify about potential rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and Process of Making Distinctness Test
rubrics_metrics.description: A process of making and a product made by the process can be distinct if (A) the process as claimed is not an obvious process of making the product and can be used to make another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of different processes or products need not be documented. A product defined by the process by which it is made is still a product claim (In re Bridgeford) and can be restricted from the process if the examiner can demonstrate the product can be made by another materially different process. If applicant convincingly traverses the requirement, the burden shifts to the examiner to document a viable alternative or withdraw the requirement. Use form paragraphs 8.18 and 8.21.04 for such restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus and Product Made Distinctness Test
rubrics_metrics.description: An apparatus and a product made by the apparatus are distinct if (A) the apparatus as claimed is not an obvious apparatus for making the product and can be used to make another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.19 for restriction between apparatus and product. The examiner must show by way of example either (A) or (B); the example need not be documented. If applicant proves the examiner's example isn't workable, the examiner must suggest another viable example or withdraw the restriction. Conclude restriction with form paragraph 8.21 and, where appropriate, follow with form paragraph 8.21.04 for potential rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and Process of Using Distinctness Test
rubrics_metrics.description: A product and a process of using the product are distinct if (A) the process of using as claimed can be practiced with another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be used in a materially different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must provide an example (not required to be documented). If applicant convincingly argues the suggested alternative use cannot be accomplished, the burden is on the examiner to support another viable alternative or withdraw the requirement. Use form paragraphs 8.20 and 8.21.04 in restriction requirements between product and method of using.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-way Product/Process-of-Making/Process-of-Using Restriction Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims to product, process of making, and process of using are all present, a three-way requirement for restriction can only be made where the process of making is distinct from the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the process of making and the product are not distinct, the process of using may be joined with the product and the process of making even if a distinctness showing between the product and process of using exists. Applicant may be required to elect the product and process of making or the process of using. Use form paragraph 8.20 where appropriate and see MPEP § 821.04 for rejoinder practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Products/Processes Distinctness Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For related product or related process inventions, inventions are distinct only if (A) the inventions as claimed do not overlap in scope (mutually exclusive), (B) the inventions as claimed are not obvious variants, and (C) the inventions are either not capable of use together or can have a materially different design, mode of operation, function, or effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden is on the examiner to provide an example to support distinctness (example need not be documented). If applicant proves the examiner's example is not workable, the examiner must suggest another viable example or withdraw the restriction. See MPEP § 806.05(j) and form paragraph 8.14.01 for restriction between related products/processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate-Final Product Distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: An intermediate product and a final product can be distinct inventions if the intermediate product is useful to make other than the final product and the species are patentably distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically the intermediate loses its identity in the final product; demonstrate intermediate utility to make other than the final product to prove distinctness. Use form paragraph 8.14 for intermediate-final product restriction and conclude with form paragraph 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Inventions Definition and Restriction Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions as claimed are independent if there is no disclosed relationship between them (they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect). If independent inventions exist and there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required, applicant should be required to restrict claims to one of the independent inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: unrelated items (apparel vs locomotive bearing), unrelated processes (painting house vs boring well). For process/apparatus, if apparatus cannot be used to practice the process (or any part), they are independent. Use form paragraphs 8.20.02 or 8.20.03 as applicable and conclude with form paragraph 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrelated Inventions Formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are unrelated if they are not disclosed as capable of use together and have different designs, modes of operation, and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.20.02 (or 8.20.03 for unrelated product and process) to document restriction between unrelated inventions; must be followed by form paragraph 8.21. Insert reasons for concluding inventions are unrelated in bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Must State Reasons (No Mere Conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every restriction requirement must include particular reasons (not merely a statement of conclusion) why each invention is independent or distinct and why there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, for combination/subcombination relationships the examiner should explain why the subcombination has utility by itself or in other combinations and why the combination does not require the particulars of the subcombination. Form paragraphs 8.01, 8.02, and 8.14–8.20.02 may be used to explain distinctness or independence. See MPEP §§ 806.05–806.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species Independence and Election Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is no disclosure of a relationship between species, they are independent and restriction may be permissible if patentable differences exist and there would be a serious burden on the examiner. If a disclosed relationship exists, the disclosed relation must be discussed and reasons advanced that it does not prevent restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must elect a single disclosed species under 35 U.S.C. 121 when restriction is required, even if applicant disagrees. Election should not be required between species that are clearly unpatentable over each other; examiner should group clearly unpatentable species together. Election may be required prior to a search in applications with multiple species and no generic claims, or with both species and generic/Markush claims. Use MPEP §§ 803, 809, 821.04 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing Examiner's Burden for Insisting on Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: To justify insisting upon restriction, the examiner must explain why there would be a serious burden if restriction is not required by showing one of: (A) separate classification; (B) separate status in the art when classifiable together; or (C) a different field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate classification shows recognition in the art as separate subjects and separate fields of search (patents need not be cited). Separate status in the art may be shown by citing patents as evidence. A different field of search exists where searching for one invention would not likely find art pertinent to the other (different classes/subclasses, resources, queries). If classification and field of search are the same and no clear indication of separate future classification exists, no reasons exist for division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Claims and Their Effect on Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims (e.g., genus claims linking species or subcombination claims linking plural combinations) if allowable, act to prevent restriction between otherwise divisible inventions by requiring rejoinder of the linked inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking claims and inventions they link are usually all products or all processes. Linking claims must be examined with the elected invention and are considered part of the elected invention. When all claims directed to the elected invention are allowable and a linking claim is allowable, the restriction must be withdrawn and previously withdrawn nonelected claims that depend from or require all limitations of the allowable linking claim must be rejoined and fully examined. If previously withdrawn claims were canceled by applicant, they may be reinstated by amendment upon allowance of linking claim(s). See MPEP § 821.04 for rejoinder practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Example Requirement and Burden Shifting
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner asserts distinctness (material differences, alternate uses, etc.), the examiner must show by appropriate explanation and, where required, provide an example to support distinctness; the example need not be documented. If applicant proves or provides convincing argument that the examiner's example or suggested alternative use is not workable, the burden shifts to the examiner to suggest another viable example or withdraw the restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This burden-shifting principle recurs across process/apparatus, apparatus/product, product/process-of-using, and related-inventions contexts. Examiners should provide reasons and examples; applicants may rebut with proof or convincing argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Potential Rejoinder of Process Claims (8.21.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: When restriction is required between product/apparatus and process claims, the examiner must notify applicant that if product/apparatus claims are found allowable, withdrawn process claims that include all limitations of the allowable product/apparatus claim should be considered for rejoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejoined process claims will be fully examined for patentability (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112). Withdrawn process claims not commensurate in scope with an allowable product/apparatus claim will not be rejoined. Applicant is advised to amend process claims during prosecution to require the limitations of product/apparatus claims to facilitate rejoinder; failure to do so may result in no rejoinder. Note prohibition against double patenting rejections of 35 U.S.C. 121 does not apply where restriction is withdrawn before patent issues. Use form paragraph 8.21.04 at the end of restriction requirements between process and product/apparatus or product and process of using.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species Procedure and Required Contents of Reply
rubrics_metrics.description: When election of species is required, the examiner should identify generic claims (or lack thereof), clearly identify disclosed species (preferably by figures/examples or distinguishing characteristics), provide reasons why species are independent or distinct, and require applicant to elect a single disclosed species under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete reply should include a proper election along with a listing of all claims readable on the elected species, including any claims subsequently added. In cases where restriction accompanies action on elected claims, that action will be considered an action on the merits and the next action may be made final where appropriate. For treatment of nonelected claims see MPEP § 821 et seq. Use form paragraph 8.01 (Election of Species; Species Claim(s) Present) with bracket fields for species and reasons.
